newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank welcomes Moody's upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank welcomes Moody's upgrade.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank, which has spent the past few weeks defending its markets from speculators, on Monday warmly welcomed Moody's Investors Service report upgrading the country's banks and sovereign debt.

"The upgrade represents a vote of further confidence by Moody's on the sustainability of the strong Philippine economic growth, underpinned by structural reforms, buoyant exports and fiscal and monetary discipline," central bank governor Gabriel Singson said.
Moody's earlier announced it had upgraded the Philippines' foreign currency sovereign ceiling for government bonds and notes, and lifted the ratings on 11 major banks.
The central bank has boosted interest rates and intervened heavily in the currency market to defend the peso from the spillover of Thailand's economic woes.
Share prices have fallen sharply since last month, initially on fears the banking and property sectors were facing a Thai-style crisis.

"The upgrade also means that perceptive analysts could discern the strengths of an emerging market like the Philippines beyond the fashionable headlines of today that cater to fears fuelled by knee-jerk reactions and superficial comparisons," Singson said.
